why: A camera whose *sensor* turns the picture, so R-CTL-15's other half can be photographed.
R-CTL-15 asks the console to say which of the two is turning the picture, because the two
are identical in the picture and not in their cost: the board's is processing on every
frame, the sensor's is free. That is two sentences on the page, and a gate that only ever
photographs one of them is a gate that would not notice the other going wrong.
**No camera on the bench can draw the sensor's sentence.** The Global Shutter Camera
implements no `horizontal_flip`, no `vertical_flip` and no `rotate` — that is the recorded
answer in `camera-globalshutter.json` and it is why `video/orientation.ts` exists at all —
so the sensor path has no hardware here to exercise it. This file is the only way to draw
it, and it says so rather than pretending a device answered.
**An overlay, not a second camera.** `capabilities` below replaces those three keys on the
recorded fixture's own `found[0]` and nothing else: same device, same card, same by-path
name, same formats, same eighteen other controls. Kept as an overlay so the recorded
answers stay in exactly one file — a whole second copy would drift from the board's the
first time either was regenerated, and would do it silently. `verify-pages.sh` is what
merges the two.
**The ranges are what a UVC camera that implements these controls reports**: each flip is
a switch (`min=0 max=1 step=1`), and `rotate` is degrees in steps of 90. `current` is 1 on
`horizontal_flip` because the recorded fixture's camera asks for a mirror, and a control
the sensor holds is drawn from the device's own read-back rather than from what was stored
(R-CTL-10) — so a page that drew the stored value instead would photograph identically
here and differ the moment the two disagree, which is the whole point of the distinction.
Nothing on the bench has answered any of this. It is a shape a camera can have, not a
measurement, and no page drawn from it may be reported as hardware evidence.
